cases.name: Sophie Sergie
cases.about: She was a student at the at the University of Alaska Fairbanks. Sophie studied marine biology and worked as a teacher’s assistant at the Pitkas Point School. Sergie was from the Native village of Pitkas Point in western Alaska.
cases.caseStatus: COLD CASE SOLVED; CONVICTION; FORENSIC INVESTIGATIVE GENETIC GENEALOGY SOLVED
cases.narrative: On 4/26/1993, she was found sexually assaulted, stabbed and shot in the second floor women’s restroom of Bartlett Hall, University of Alaska Fairbanks. Sergie had been sexually assaulted, stabbed multiple times on her face and shot in the back of the head at close range.

cases.name: Velma Pungowiyi Koontz
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "While working as a teachers aide in Savoonga she met and married her husband Keith Koontz on February 29th, 1968. She spent her early married life living on a trapline on Beaver Creek, and spent time living in Savoonga, Bethel and settled in Two Rivers where she and Keith built their log home.

Velma often talked of loving memories of ice skating for the first time at camp and dog sled rides from camp to Savoonga. Velma was an excellent skin sewer and enjoyed listening to live music, and playing card games. She was a devoted sister, wife, mother, grandmother and Baha'i. She welcomed and embraced people from all different backgrounds and races and was quick to defend anyone who faced discrimination. Velma was also well traveled. She made three trips to the Baha'i Shrines in Haifa Israel where tourists once asked if she and Keith were members of the Beatles! She also visited Italy, France, Germany, Mexico, Greenland, Denmark, and Iran. Her grandfather was the first Christian on St. Lawrence Island and Velma was the first to embrace the Baha'i Faith."
cases.narrative: She was found shot in the back of the head in her wheelchair.
